title:
PROBABILITY,
(CONDITIONAL PROBABILITY AND VENN DIAGRAMS)
objective: LO: I can use Venn diagrams to find conditional probabilities.

content.text: Conditional probability is the probability of an event occurring given that another event has already occurred. Written P(A|B) meaning 'probability of A given B'.
A Venn diagram shows overlapping sets. The intersection shows elements in both sets.

examples.expr: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)

examples.desc: that is for independent events only
union means in A OR B or both

key_idea.title: Key idea
key_idea.text: P(A|B) means restrict to only those outcomes in B, then find how many are also in A.
key_idea.caption: Restrict the sample space to B

modelled_examples.label: Example 1 – from a Venn diagram
modelled_examples.question: In a class: 12 play football, 8 play tennis, 5 play both, 30 total. Find P(football | tennis).
modelled_examples.explanation: Given they play tennis (8 people), how many also play football (5).

modelled_examples.label: Example 2 – P(A or B)
modelled_examples.question: Using the same data, find P(football or tennis).
steps: P(F or T) = P(F) + P(T) − P(F and T)
modelled_examples.explanation: Subtract the intersection to avoid counting it twice.

modelled_examples.label: Example 3 – neither event
modelled_examples.question: Find P(neither football nor tennis).
modelled_examples.explanation: Subtract those in at least one set from the total.

modelled_examples.label: Example 4 – given information
modelled_examples.question: P(A) = 0.6, P(B) = 0.4, P(A and B) = 0.2. Find P(B|A).
modelled_examples.explanation: Divide the intersection probability by the condition probability.

practice.heading: Reading Venn diagrams
practice.instruction: A Venn diagram shows: A only = 7, B only = 5, A and B = 3, neither = 5. Total = 20.

practice.heading: Conditional probability
practice.instruction: Using the same data: A only = 7, B only = 5, both = 3, neither = 5.

practice.heading: Two-way tables to Venn diagrams
practice.instruction: 60 students: 25 study French, 20 study Spanish, 10 study both.

questions.expression: P(A) = 0.7, P(A and B) = 0.35. Find P(B|A).
P(B) = 0.4, P(A|B) = 0.5. Find P(A and B).
100 people: 40 like tea, 30 like coffee, 15 like both. P(tea|coffee)?

P(pass|revised) = 0.9, P(revised) = 0.6. Find P(pass and revised).

items.statement: P(A|B) means the probability of A given B has occurred
P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) − P(A and B)
In a Venn diagram, the intersection shows elements in both sets

problems.text: In a school, 70% of students have a phone, 50% have a tablet, and 30% have both. A student is chosen at random. Given they have a phone, what is the probability they also have a tablet?

A medical test is 95% accurate (P(positive|disease) = 0.95). The disease affects 1% of the population. If a person tests positive, what is P(disease|positive)? (Hint: consider false positives with P(positive|no disease) = 0.05.)
